{{Short description|American chemist}}
{{COI|date=May 2019}}'''Charles R. Martin''' (born November 20, 1959) is an American Distinguished Professor of chemistry at [[University of Florida]]. He is a [[Nanotechnology]] expert and a pioneer of membrane-based template synthesis of [[nanomaterials]].<ref name="E&CN news">{{cite journal|last=ROUHI|first=A. MAUREEN|journal=C&EN|date=June 2001|volume=29|pages=29–33|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/coverstory/7924/7924nanotubules.html|issn=0009-2347|doi=10.1021/cen-v079n024.p029|issue=24|title=From Membranes to Nanotubules|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He is listed as one of the World's Top 100 Chemists of the past decade (2000–2010) by Thomson Reuters.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thomson Reuters World's Top 100 Chemists of the past decade (2000–2010)|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/}}</ref>  He is also a musician and songwriter in [[Gainesville, Florida]].<ref name=Alligator>{{cite news|title=UF chemistry professor to release solo album "Genius Boy Music"|url=http://m.alligator.org/news/campus/article_2bf7b248-4058-11e3-9573-001a4bcf887a.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131209203508/http://m.alligator.org/news/campus/article_2bf7b248-4058-11e3-9573-001a4bcf887a.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2013|date=2013-10-29}}</ref>

== Education and academic career ==

=== Education ===
Martin graduated with high distinction from [[Centre College]] of [[Kentucky]] in 1975 and was elected to [[Phi Beta Kappa]]. He obtained a Ph.D. in analytical chemistry in 1980 under the direction of Prof. Henry Freiser. He was a Robert A. Welch Postdoctoral Fellow with Prof. [[Allen J. Bard]] in [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]] at Austin.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=CV of Prof.Martin|url=http://www.chem.ufl.edu/~crmartin/Group%20Members%20Images/CRM%20CV%209-09.pdf}}</ref>

=== Research in Texas A&M University ===
Martin began his academic career as an assistant professor in [[Texas A%26M University|Texas A&M university]] in 1981. He became the first person to get tenure as an analytical chemist{{dubious|date=August 2014}}. He became a full professor in 1990. Beginning in the 1980s, his research group pioneered a versatile method for preparing [[nanomaterials]] called template synthesis. This synthesis method is now used in laboratories throughout the world.<ref name=Penner>{{cite journal|last=Penner|first=Reginald|author2=Charles martin|title=Preparation and Electrochemical Characterization of Ultramicroelectrode Ensembles|journal=Anal Chem|date=November 1987|pages=2625–2630|doi=10.1021/ac00148a020|volume=59|issue=21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ran Liu Group page|url=http://research.chem.psu.edu/axsgroup/Ran/research/templatesynthesis.html|access-date=2013-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216155221/http://research.chem.psu.edu/axsgroup/Ran/research/templatesynthesis.html|archive-date=2013-12-16|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Doerr|first=Allison|title=Chemical nano-corking|journal=Nature Methods|date=May 2006|volume=3|url=http://www.cienciaviva.pt/rede/oceanos/2desafio/22.pdf|doi=10.1038/nmeth0506-338a|pmid=16685787|issue=5|pages=338|s2cid=30722464 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211184742/http://www.cienciaviva.pt/rede/oceanos/2desafio/22.pdf|archivedate=2013-12-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Siwy Research Lab|url=http://www.physics.uci.edu/~zsiwy/}}</ref>

=== Research in Colorado State University ===
In 1990, Martin moved to [[Colorado State University]]. He used the template synthesis method to fabricate nanotubes and nanowires of a wide range of materials. Many important applications such as separation, electrochemical energy storage, and electrochemical analysis have been explored.<ref name=CV />

=== Research in University of Florida ===
Martin moved to [[University of Florida]] in 1999. He is currently the Colonel Allan R. and Margaret G. Crow Professor of Chemistry in University of Florida. He became University Distinguished Professor in 2006, one of only 70 University Professorships in UF.<ref name=DP>{{cite web|title=UF Distinguished Professors|url=http://fora.aa.ufl.edu/provost/IndependentFora/Distinguished-Professors}}</ref> Martin's current research interests are applications of template-prepared nanotubes and nanotube membranes in biosensing and electrochemistry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Martin Research Group|url=http://www.chem.ufl.edu/~crmartin/research.htm}}</ref>

== Awards and achievement ==
Among his Awards, Martin was the recipient of the Carl Wagner Memorial Award of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (1999),<ref>{{cite web|title=Past Carl Wagner Award recipients|url=http://www.electrochem.org/awards/ecs/recipients/c_wagner_recipients.htm}}</ref> The Florida Award of the [[American Chemical Society|Florida ACS]] (2005),<ref>{{cite web|title=PREVIOUS FLORIDA AWARD RECIPIENTS|url=http://www.fame.chem.ufl.edu/flaward.html|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130922024812/http://www.fame.chem.ufl.edu/flaward.html|archivedate=2013-09-22}}</ref> Fellow of Electrochemical Society (2005),<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows of The Electrochemical Society|url=http://www.electrochem.org/awards/ecs/recipients/fellow_recipients.htm}}</ref> Nano 50 Innovator Award from Nanotech Briefs (2007),<ref>{{cite web|title=Nano 50 Innovators Award 2007 recipients|url=http://www.owlnet.rice.edu/~rv4/Ajayan/nano50.pdf|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100621160455/http://www.owlnet.rice.edu/~rv4/Ajayan/nano50.pdf|archivedate=2010-06-21}}</ref> the Charles N. Reilley Award of the Society for Electroanalytical Chemistry (2009),<ref>{{cite web|title=List of recipients|url=http://electroanalytical.org/awards.html|access-date=2013-11-08|archive-date=2018-04-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403234829/http://electroanalytical.org/awards.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the American Chemical Society Division of Analytical Chemistry Award in Electrochemistry (2010).<ref>{{cite web|title=List of past recipients|url=http://www.analyticalsciences.org/awards.php#Electrochemistry|access-date=2013-11-08|archive-date=2013-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215012609/http://www.analyticalsciences.org/awards.php#Electrochemistry|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Music ==
Besides his academic success, Martin is a musician and songwriter in Gainesville Florida. He had four albums with bands ''dblWiDE'' and ''The Righteous Kind'' and the solo album ''Genius Boy Music'' was released on November 22, 2013.<ref name=Alligator />
